title: Intraday Hunter process quizzes
disclaimer: Educational self-check only. Not SEBI advice.

questions.prompt: Inventory = buyers sitting. Open = solid gap-up. What is the matrix bias?
choices: BUY — go with the market; don’t target those buyers
SELL — harvest the buyers immediately
FLAT — wait for afternoon
SELL — temptation trap on every gap-up
questions.explanation: When buyers are sitting and the open is a solid gap-up, §4 says BUY with the market. Targeting buyers on a strong gap-up is the wrong branch.

questions.prompt: Inventory = buyers sitting. Open = flat / gap-down. Default map?
choices: BUY breakout continuation
SELL — target the sitting buyers
FLAT always — no plan exists
Chase the first green candle
questions.explanation: Soft open with buyers still inside → sell-the-buyers is the default (P8). Seen on 07-28 and 07-30.

questions.prompt: After holiday + recovery, inventory often looks cleared. Gap-up open — what’s the process read?
choices: Free long — leftover shorts must cover forever
Temptation-trap risk → often SELL late FOMO buyers
Always FLAT until next week
Average into any red candle
questions.explanation: P6 / 07-27: holiday/recovery clears short inventory; gap-up can tempt late buyers, then reject — not a free long.

questions.prompt: You cannot cleanly tag buyer vs seller inventory. Market has been covering/holding for days. Best default?
choices: Invent a counter-short for excitement
Follow the active regime (cover/recovery → buy bias)
Force a range scalp every open
Ignore companions and trade only one index
questions.explanation: P11 / 07-29: unclear inventory → follow what’s already happening. Don’t invent a counter-trade.

questions.prompt: You planned to sell sitting buyers, but the open is a huge runaway green gap-up. Action?
choices: Chase puts harder — bigger gap, bigger edge
NO TRADE / stay away — don’t chase the runaway
Double size longs to ride FOMO
Enter at open with no stop
questions.explanation: P14 / 07-30 / §4: avoid runaway gap-up chases even when the soft-open sell plan was your preferred map.

questions.prompt: 07-27 pre: strong bounce after a very negative backdrop into holiday. What inventory read did he emphasize?
choices: Fresh buyers flooding in forever
Bounce buyers likely booked; sellers may still sit — or inventory cleared into holiday
Guaranteed clear_buyers regime for a week
Only Nifty inventory matters
questions.explanation: Post confirmed holiday+recovery → don’t assume short inventory still sitting; gap-up became a temptation trap sell.

questions.prompt: 07-28 (BN/Nifty expiry): BN held above 57k, companions positive, soft gap-down. Live action matched which plan?
choices: Buy the dip with calls and hold through expiry crush
Sell / puts — target sitting buyers on the soft open
No trade because expiry forbids all entries
Short only Sensex, ignore BN
questions.explanation: Soft open + buyers sitting → sell-the-buyers. Expiry meant book sooner (premium crush risk).

questions.prompt: 07-29: inventory unclear, large gap-up with mild rejection. What did he do?
choices: Short the gap because rejection candles looked scary
Follow ongoing cover → bought calls; watched for fast rejection risk
Stay flat all day with no thesis
Average puts after every bounce
questions.explanation: Unclear inventory → follow active cover regime. Gap size still raises trap risk even on a buy bias (P12).

questions.prompt: 07-30 (Sensex expiry): multi-day buyers likely sitting; open almost flat / slight gap-down. Default map?
choices: Sell setups targeting multi-day buyers
Must buy because prior day was green
Wait for a huge green runaway before acting
Trade only after 2pm
questions.explanation: Multi-day bid + soft open → harvest buyers. Huge runaway would have been avoid (P14).

questions.prompt: 07-31 range day: what does a sudden large sell at the open imply?
choices: Automatic buy-the-dip
Range warning — bad for forced longs
Guaranteed trend day down with no risk
Ignore companions forever
questions.explanation: P15: on range/shrinking-momentum days, large open sell is a range warning — don’t force longs.

questions.prompt: 08-03: multi-day buying context, solid gap-up, then light rejection/chop. Correct process?
choices: Target buyers with puts because any rejection kills longs
Don’t target buyers — buy with market; light rejection ≠ deep liquidation
Exit instantly on first red tick
Hold one index forever until companions catch up
questions.explanation: P18: gap-up + multi-day buyers — light/slow rejection often = Friday booking, not thesis kill. He bought with the open.

questions.prompt: You’ve booked a decent average target; tape turns sideways/slow with lots of time left. Best action?
choices: Hold for a ‘big’ day that might still come
Exit — sideways after decent profit is an exit cue
Average more size into the chop
Ignore expiry pressure always
questions.explanation: P13 / §7: sideways after decent profit → exit; don’t wait for a fantasy extension.

questions.prompt: Only Bank Nifty worked to a known target; Sensex/Nifty lagged and path beyond the setup is unclear. Rule?
choices: Invent a larger target and overhold for confirmation
Book the mapped path; wait for a new opportunity
Revenge-enter the opposite side immediately
Move stop to zero and hope
questions.explanation: P7 + P20 / 08-03: one index alone → don’t overhold; book when you leave the mapped path.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid FLAT / no-trade condition from the bible?
choices: Inventory unknown and you refuse to follow regime, or sideways grind with no unlocked branch
Any red candle in the first minute
Whenever Nifty and BN differ by 1 point
Only after you already lost money
questions.explanation: §10: allow_trade false, sideways grind, messy small gap-down with no plan, runaway gaps, unknown inventory without follow-regime — return FLAT.

questions.prompt: Solid gap-up long thesis. Open shows light, slow rejection. How to read it?
choices: Real liquidation — cut all longs immediately always
Weak Friday / short-term booking — long thesis can stay valid
Proof inventory was sellers sitting
Signal to chase puts with no stop
questions.explanation: §5 rejection filter + P18: light/slow rejection after solid gap-up ≠ deep long liquidation. Fast large selling is the real warning.

questions.prompt: Which permanent rule matches: soft open + buyers sitting → sell-the-buyers default?
choices: P3
P8
questions.explanation: P8 is the soft-open sell-the-buyers default (07-28, 07-30).

questions.prompt: For options buying, the bible prioritizes:
choices: Tiny SL + 1:10 fantasy targets
Accuracy via root reading + sensible RR (~1:1)
Always 1:5 regardless of process
No stops — only targets
questions.explanation: P3 / §8: options prefer accuracy + ~1:1 RR; time decay fights tiny-SL fantasy targets.

questions.prompt: 08-03 lesson on edge quality: what kills the edge after a good gap-up long?
choices: Any companion lag of a few points
Continuous upside without pause (that’s the edge)
A stall that fills late buyers and invites reversal
Booking at a known target
questions.explanation: P19: edge needs continuous momentum; stall invites late buyers and your trade can reverse.

questions.prompt: Flush-then-cover buy thesis: market sells straight through your hold assumption / loss limit. Next step?
choices: Average more — the cover ‘must’ return
Exit — don’t think a dead thesis back to life
Widen stop without a new plan
Switch to investing timeframe mid-trade
questions.explanation: P16 / 07-31: flush-then-cover needs the hold; sell-through → exit. Wrong trade + accelerating adverse = cut.

questions.prompt: Bot rule for extending targets requires:
choices: Any single index printing a new high
companion_bias aligned with trade direction
Expiry day always means max target
Ignoring Sensex completely
questions.explanation: §6: extend_target only if companions align with the trade. One index alone → take known target (P7).
